rv.q: Presley, the poor boy who reinvented himself, was an admirer of the 26th president of the US, a sickly rich kid who grew into a manly man accruing more privilege along the way.

At times it’s a bit muddled and with so much crammed into 100 minutes, maybe a little pruning would have resulted in a more cohesive message and a more satisfying theatrical experience for the audience.

cn.t: This experimental two-hander about desire and identity through Elvis impersonation earns mixed-to-positive reviews for its high-concept playfulness with gender and myth, though some find its approach more clever than compelling.
